lines.en: I peer up at the sky through a break in the trees and find a moment of comfort in convincing myself I’m not surrounded when I know I really am.
That, too, is somewhat poetic. Yet less so than it would be to die in the same way that I was more symbolically killed many, many years ago.
There’s poetry in everything, though.
That’s something I’ve believed forever.
But I often find myself wondering whether I believe that because it’s what’s real to me or because it’s what someone else made me see after peeling away the covers.
And I often find myself wondering if those two thoughts are mutually exclusive because there’s a fine line between reality and what’s really real, you know?
It’s interesting how deeply the people we look up to when we’re young are able to affect us, isn’t it?
And how, despite all the adversity and turmoil in the face of those teachings, changing at all when you get to my age seems nigh impossible.
Ami’s still young. So, if I want to mold her world, I need to do it now.
Because waiting any longer not only runs the risk of ill-preparing her for what surely awaits us in this infinite life of ours-
But runs the risk of turning her into an actual monster who will pry open my ribcage before ripping my heart out and swallowing it whole.
Girls these days will do crazy things for sustenance, you know. Or perhaps even leisure if you want to make her out to be even worse than she actually is.
But I know the truth.
She’s just broken and in love. And the two of those things can easily drive us mad on their own.
When they’re combined, though?...
: Yo!
When they’re combined, there’s nothing that can stop the metamorphosis other than someone who exhibits the same symptoms.

As much as I’d love to inform you of our proper diagnoses, I’m afraid there’s not a doctor in the world we could pay to make sense of how our insides look or how they communicate with and respond to one another.
I just know that they do.
So maybe that’s “love” working its magic again. Or maybe it’s just the worm.
Whatever it is, though- know this one thing for sure.
Our time is numbered.
This will almost certainly be fatal.
: Took you guys long enough. Been waitin’ here for like an hour already.
: I’m surprised your bike even made it here. I kind of assumed you’d just be hiking or something.
: Nah, I just brought my crappy old one. Had to drag it through a few puddles on the way over, but it got here in one piece either way.
: Sensei, who is that? She looks...kind of familiar.
: Yumi’s mom. You’ve probably seen her at Sara’s bar for one of the parties.
: Call it by its proper name! My ancestors didn’t come up with such a great pun just for it to be ignored by someone with no sense of humor!
: I’m Yuki. Ami, right?
: Oh, yeah. Sorry. It’s...nice to meet you?
: Likewise. Sorry if my daughter’s ever picked on you before. Which she probably has because she’s a fuckin’ bitch.
: Are you staying the night, Yuki? We’re giving Sensei and Ami the second tent, which means the rest of us will have to get kind of close.
: Wasn’t plannin’ on it, but now I definitely ain’t plannin’ on it. Y’all can enjoy your fuckin’ slumber party on your own. I’m just gonna head back and crash once it gets dark.
: Worth a shot.
: Are you sure, Yuki? We don’t open back up until tomorrow night, so it’s not like you have anywhere to be unless you have a secret Yakuza boyfriend you haven’t told any of us about.
: Just because the only dude I’ve ever been with was in the Yakuza doesn’t mean that’s my type, you know. I can like normal dudes.
: So you have a normal boyfriend instead?
: Sure. Yeah.
: What’s his name?! When can we meet him?!
: It’s that guy right there. We got together for Yumi’s sake and he just finished movin’ into my place. Got a dog and everything, which means we’re basically a real family now.
: Please don’t make jokes like that in front of Ami or you’ll wind up waking up with fewer body parts than you’re accustomed to.
: Damn, now I definitely ain’t sleepin’ here.
A brief argument about my relationship status subsequently takes place, but I decide to black most of it out as I can tell it’s making Ami uncomfortable.
I can tell this entire trip is making Ami uncomfortable. But it’s not like I didn’t expect that to happen. And, to be completely honest, I’m probably even more uncomfortable than she is.
Like, I’m having sex with all of these girls apart from Yuki and that could spiral into something horrible pretty quickly if I say or do just one thing wrong.
Like, every single one of these girls wants to fuck me except Yuki (maybe) and I’ve yet to touch any of them, so I’m practically a sitting duck out here.
But I don’t matter today — and that’s saying a lot as someone who’s practically the symbol of self-loathing narcissism.
I’ll just stick to my guns and try to not let anything put me on the back foot for the next twenty-four hours so I can focus more on Ami.
: So! Wanna go for a walk, big dog?
: Please never call me “big dog” again. I was quite literally just thinking about how I don’t want anything to put me on my back foot so I can focus on Ami.
: Then I’ve got extra bad news for you since I’m going to kidnap her now.
: Why is everything I don’t want to happen suddenly happening in very quick succession? Are even my inner monologues not safe anymore?
lmaoooooooooo
Oh, come on.
: You’re kidnapping me?
: Yeah! Let’s go set up your tent while Maki and Haru-chan put the other one together. Then, after that, I can show you a trick that’ll help you get rid of those dark circles.
: I don’t think-
: We’ve got a long day ahead of us, Sensei. It’s probably best to just let Sara get all of her motherly energy out of the way now since her daughter’s not here to serve as the outlet for that.
: Just not that kind of motherly energy.
: No one said anything about that kind of motherly energy, Maki.
: But we were all thinking it.
: We most certainly were not.
: I was.
: You were?
: See?
: I admit defeat. I have underestimated the depravity of this group. Which, in hindsight, was extremely foolish of me.
And doubly foolish as she is essentially my sex-slave now and would suck me off in front of everyone here with just the snap of my fingers.
: The fuck’s even goin’ on right now?
: Don’t worry about it, Yuki. If Maki keeps talking, her words will sully your status as the most innocent woman here.
: There’s a friggin’ teenager here. Ain’t no way I’m more “innocent” than her.
If only she knew.
: Uh...Sana’s mom? Can we-
: Stop calling me that! Just Sara is fine. Or Mom! Or Mama. Or Mommy.
: Actually, no. Mommy might be kind of weird. But the others are-
: Sara...do we really need to do this now? I’m...okay with spending time with you, of course. But right now, I want to-

: Shh! It’s fine! We can get to know each other a little better while your uncle explains the different types of motherly energy to Yuki — a woman who, despite being a mother, is unfamiliar with all of them.
: You really gonna throw shade at me all casually like that? I’ve barely even said shit.
: Is there a reason you want to go for a walk? Because, if not, I kind of want to stay here and make sure Sara doesn’t force Ami to sign any adoption papers.
: Now just sign here and-
: Yoink.
: Noooo! My newest daughter!
: There’s somethin’ I wanna talk about, but I ain’t good at doin’ that shit in front of other people. Shouldn’t take long, though. You can get right back to chaperoning your niece in a few minutes.
: Then, I guess it can’t be helped.
: I’ll be right back, Ami. Just humor Sara for now.
: If...that’s what you think is best...
Yuki leads me into the woods and given that she is much stronger and more intimidating than me, I can’t help but trick myself into thinking I’m about to be mugged for everything I’ve got.
Which isn’t much, to be honest.
But she could probably fetch a pretty penny for auctioning off my niece to some underground organization specializing in human trafficking or the selective breeding of redheads.
I doubt Sara would be in on that, though. She seems to like young girls a little too much to try shipping any of them off.
Which kind of sucks for Haruka if you think about it. Because she likes them a lot too, but in a completely different way.
So yeah, that’s what I’m thinking about as we move further into the woods.
But, of course, Yuki is thinking about something completely different.
: Sara tells me you’re lookin’ to be like more of a dad to Ami or some shit?
: Do secrets just not exist to women or something?
: That shit don’t exist to anybody, man. Sure you’d be gossipin’ with your guy friends too if you weren’t a creep who only hung out with people who have vaginas.
: Well, forgive me but my options are pretty limited in a city where men basically just don’t exist.
: You’re right, though.
: I doubt much would change even if they did.
: Ain’t nothin’ wrong with sharin’ secrets so long as it gets more people on your side, I think. And Sara only told me to begin with since I’m goin’ through the same shit with Yumi right now.
: You are?
: Yeah. Tryin’ to, at least. But it ain’t exactly easy when I’ve been even more absent than you’ve been for the entire time you’ve known Ami.

: Which means you’ve still got the benefit of havin’ her like you and that’s a thing I ain’t ever had. But I also get that shit’s probably a little more confusing on account of you not bein’ her actual dad in the first place.
: So that’s why you wanted to go for a walk? Are we going to give each other tips on how to be bad parents?
: That ain’t it, man. Just want you to know that I understand what you’re goin’ through and that it’s totally fine if all of this makes you feel like shit.
: Knowin’ you failed somebody you could have turned into a great person stings. And it sucks extra hard because that shit just hits you outta nowhere sometimes.

: Like, I ain’t gonna lie, there were long periods where I forgot I even had a daughter. But bein’ around her again has been makin’ me realize just how fuckin’ dumb I was to not, like...keep her in my thoughts, you know?
: Do you love her?
: Love, huh?
: Yeah.
: Do you love Ami?
: I do.
: How do you know that? Like...what’s different about the way you look at her than you would look at somebody like Sara or...any of your other friends I don’t know shit about?
: I think it comes down to how much pain you’re willing to withstand to prevent that person from going through the same thing.
: Does it really work that way?
: No. But I still think that’s a good way to measure it. So, if you’d be willing to hurt yourself in exchange for Yumi’s continued “happiness,” I don’t think it’s crazy to say you love her.
: See, that’s where shit gets hard though, isn’t it? Because you and me don’t really give a fuck about ourselves.

: But at least you’re healthy and shit. I’ll be lucky to get another ten years outta life with how much smoking and drinking I do. And that ain’t even countin’ all the doping I did the last couple decades.
: So yeah, I’d be fine with gettin’ hurt if it’d prevent Yumi from feelin’ that shit. But I’d probably do the same thing for you as well and I sure as fuck don’t love you.
: Maybe you do?
: That boyfriend joke from earlier go to your head or something?
: Maybe. Or maybe I just liked the idea of being a real family and want to hear your daughter call me Daddy?
: I’m just gonna go ahead and pretend you meant that in the less creepy way.
: You took that better than I thought, so maybe you don’t love her after all?
: Maybe I do, maybe I don’t. Shit’s complicated. Can’t really make sense of how I actually feel.
: But I’ve been seein’ her more often lately...
: I buy extra shit for her when I go to the store now.
: Even text her to see if she wants to get dinner or some shit a few nights outta the week. And, you know...sometimes she does. And I like that.

: But it feels fuckin’ weird because, like...why? Why’s she still showin’ me kindness like that after all the shit I put her through? Cause if my parents pulled that shit with me, ain’t no way I’d crash on their couch.
: Probably because she loves you.
: Yumi doesn’t love me. She’s smarter than that.
: Love isn’t really something you can apply logic to, Yuki.
: You think?
: Probably.
: I’m also kind of in the dark when it comes to that.
: But right now, what matters most to me is making sure that Ami doesn’t wind up feeling like this one day. And I think you’re doing a good job of doing that same thing for Yumi.

: Truth be told, I think we’re doin’ pretty shitty jobs when push comes to shove. But in a race, it ain’t how ya start that matters, it’s how ya finish. And there ain’t no way that growin’ up isn’t a race.
: Blink once and a year goes by. Blink twice and suddenly it’s harder to breathe. Blink a third time and you’re five inches shorter.
: Life goes by too fuckin’ fast, man. And we’re terrible people for forcin’ those girls to go through it.
: Technically speaking, I’ve never brought anyone into this world. So I’m not forcing anyone to do anything.
: But I’m not helping either. And that’s what this trip is about.
: I feel you there. I tried inviting Yumi but, of course, she had other shit going on.
: She has a job now. Did you know that?
: Yeah. I ran into her the other night when I was about to jump off a bridge.
: She save you?
: In a way, maybe.
: That’s my girl.
: You could show a little more concern for me you know.
: You really think I’ve got the emotional capacity to worry about more than one person?
: Just thinkin’ about Yumi’s hard enough to-
: Woah, what the fuck? Is that Kaori over there?
: That...is Kaori. Yes.
: Did she...kidnap somebody?
: Technically? Yes. But it’s a little more complicated than that.
: Yo! Kaori!
: Who goes to the place where we are located?! Stand back or face the wrath of my liquid pepper!
: Wait...Aunt Yukiburger? And uncle Friendburgerhamfriendburgerman?!
: Why are the three minus one of you spending your unday with an S inside the town where trees live?
: Same question goes to you, yo. The fuck you doin’ out here in the woods with a kid?
: Hello, Nao. Cool frog.
: This is no childburger, it is Nao-chan. And I am her mothermom, which makes you her motheraunt.
: It makes me what?
: Motherauntmomburgermomyuki.
: Nao doesn’t speak. And if you feel a strange, otherworldly presence emanating from her, you are not alone for I, too, feel that way.
: So Kaori kidnapped a mute kid and dragged her into the woods so she could play with a frog? Aight.
: Frog Boy is a living day-of-birth present. The reason we are in the same location as you is for a special human treasure hunt.
: Treasure hunt?
: It is what humans call the act of hunting for treasure.
: Friend! Surely you remember the last flattened tree corpse that sent us on a similar hunt! Do you shoelaces?!
: Was that supposed to mean “do you not?”
: I think it’d be “knot” technically.
: Thanks for the added clarity, Yuki. Conveying audio-based jokes through text boxes is hard.
: So you don’t shoelaces! Just as I presumed!
: Are you saying you got another treasure map? And that you brought Nao here to help you investigate?
: Nao-chan is correct!
: But she didn’t say anything.
: Her mouth words do not matter when her heart words are much louder! But either which way, I am excited to greet you on this day, Friend and Auntfriend!
: Treasure is easier to find when the amount of hand-arms reaching for it increases.
: Well, you have fun with that. I’m gonna go celebrate being out in the wilderness by day drinking until I have a migraine.
: Aunt Yukiburger?
: I think she just wants to relax today. But I’ll try and find the time to help you with your treasure hunt if I’m able to.
: Excellence!
: Nao-chan and I have to make nine minus three more preparations first, but we will await your un-departed departure as soon as you are shoelaces-shoelaces ready!
: In the angry-time...come, Nao-chan! I will show you the correct way to search for felinefish!

Nao excitedly hurries after her “mothermom” and the two of them disappear inside of a tent that...I’m surprised they were able to set up without the help of an actual adult rather than whatever Kaori is.
Either way, I should probably take a page out of Yuki’s book and attempt to relax as well if Sara is going to be keeping Ami occupied for the time being.
I just hope that things are going well.
I’m worried enough about her as-is and the last thing I need is today making things even harder than they’ve been lately.
I just want her to get back to normal or...something that resembles it.
Which means I need to do the same.
But that also means I have to figure out how to spend the next hour or two. That being said...
What do I want to do?
Fish with Maki
Drink with Yuki
Treasure hunt with Kaori
Call someone
Go back to the camp
